workLog.task: Audit the ADR corpus for gaps, tooling opportunities, and low-effort-model confusion
workLog.notes: Measured 98 ADRs. Findings: 59 carry no lifecycle frontmatter, so the canonical parser reported ADR-042 (the binding Python-first mandate) and ADR-005 (superseded) both as proposed; 23 records miss at least one template-required section and two incompatible structures are in use (canonical and MADR); three supersessions are one-sided; ADR-002 and ADR-039 have sat in a provisional window that expired 2026-01-17; ADR-050 mandates a deleted script; ADR-030 is not a decision record; six records are status proposed with implemented true, three of which are already enforced as binding elsewhere; ADR-055 prescribes an exception marker citing ADR-032, which governs EARS syntax; 22 files carry broken ADR links. Filed 13 issues, #5189 through #5201.

Parses only the leading frontmatter block with yaml.safe_load and returns an unknown sentinel for every undeclared state instead of failing open to proposed. Two tests in tests/skills/test_misc_skill_scripts.py encoded the old behavior; their assertions were corrected to the contract issue #5189 specifies, and a third test was added pinning that a bare status line outside frontmatter is body text. No test was skipped, disabled, or deleted.

workLog.task: Merge origin/main, fix the setup-uv SHA duplication it exposed, file #5220
workLog.notes: Merged origin/main (8 commits behind) to take the sanctioned commit-ceiling relief (20 to 40) instead of the human-only commit-limit-bypass label. The merge inherited a test red on main: Renovate #5215 bumped astral-sh/setup-uv in vendor-provenance.yml and left the old SHA restated as a literal in the test, so every future bump breaks it identically. Fixed at the duplication, asserting a 40-character SHA pin read from the workflow (universal.md MUST-8) rather than retyping the new SHA. Proven falsifiable by mutation: DEAD on astral-sh/setup-uv@v10, PASS restored, plus a probe over six regression shapes (testing.md SHOULD 17). The dorny/paths-filter SHA duplicated in test_pytest_paths_filter_covers_episodes.py was deliberately left alone: it is load-bearing, since that test models the action's internal MatchOptions and a bump genuinely invalidates the model. Separately, the merge exposed that check_branch_context hard-blocks every commit when origin/HEAD is unset, because _is_merged_history cannot resolve the trunk and the issue #3343 exemption never fires. Cleared with git remote set-head origin --auto and filed as #5220 with a two-part fix; no hook was bypassed.

workLog.task: Fix the UnicodeDecodeError family reported by Cursor Bugbot
workLog.notes: UnicodeDecodeError subclasses ValueError, so every except OSError arm around read_text let it through and one stray byte aborted the whole gate with a traceback. Reproduced before fixing. The bot named three sites; sweeping every read_text site in the PR's files found a fourth it missed, _get_dependent_adrs, and confirmed two others were already correct and must not be touched: generate_adr_index handles it at top level with ADR-035 exit 3, and check_adr_links reads with errors='replace'. Each guard was proven falsifiable by reverting it and watching the tests go dead, with a negative control in each pair that would catch an unconditional handler. The new cases pushed a test module past the 500-line ceiling and the ratchet from 574 to 575; extracted to its own module rather than suppressed, returning the ratchet to 574.

workLog.task: Merge the Bugbot autofix agent's concurrent fix
workLog.notes: The autofix agent pushed two commits fixing the same UnicodeDecodeError family while this session was fixing it. Resolved toward this branch's version, a superset: distinct messages for 'is not valid UTF-8' versus 'could not be read', comments stating why each arm exists, and nine falsifiable tests where theirs has none. The interesting failure was git's automatic merge of check_adr_lifecycle.py, which kept both their broadened arm and my narrow one, leaving the second unreachable and silently reverting the message. Three tests caught it. A test asserting only 'does not crash' would have passed the broken merge. The lesson is that when two fixes for one defect meet, the danger is the conflict git resolves silently, not the one it reports.

workLog.task: Merge origin/main and combine two competing fixes to one test
workLog.notes: PR #5219 fixed test_workflow_sets_up_uv on main while this branch carried its own fix. Each had the other's hole: #5219 asserts equality against the SHA so the next Renovate bump breaks it, and this branch searched the file as text so a stray uses: line in a comment would satisfy it. Combined: parse the job's steps, require exactly one Setup uv step, then assert its uses matches the pin shape without restating the SHA. Proven falsifiable on both axes by mutation. Both tempting resolutions were wrong, one re-introducing the drift this PR fixes and the other discarding another author's real improvement.

workLog.task: Address the Copilot review: duplicate-key class, ADR-063, template overreach
workLog.notes: Three findings worth the round. First, yaml.safe_load is last-wins on duplicate keys, so a record declaring status twice enforces one value while showing another; fixed in all three readers with the mechanism chosen per site. Second, ADR-063 had no frontmatter and relied on the whole-file regex this PR removed, so the PR silently made it unknown, and three tests missed it because each reimplemented the old regex rather than calling the parser; its docstring, its assertion and the real parser gave three different answers. Third, the template told authors not to use the ## Status section that ADR-073 explicitly retains, which is the second time this campaign turned that ADR's MAY into a directive.
